With about seven non-Li atoms per formula unit, the reaction penalty per non-Li atom may be diluted relative to simpler oxides such as Li2O.
proposals.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 and Li3BO3 proposals pointed to Li-rich, wide-gap oxyanion coatings. Their results are not shown, so this choice is a different chemical family (zirconate) that tests whether a Li-rich transition-metal oxide gives a lower penalty.

proposals.hypothesis: LiZr2(PO4)3 combines a phosphate framework, which is oxidatively robust against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V and chemically tolerant of Li6PS5Cl, with Zr4+, which resists both oxidation and reduction. It should be wide-gap and electronically insulating, and its NASICON-type structure supports Li-ion transport. It is a Zr-phosphate rather than a Ti-phosphate, so it avoids the Ti4+ reduction risk against the sulfide.
proposals.motivation: Earlier phosphate and zirconate proposals (Li3PO4 and Li-rich Zr oxides) were judged promising for this interface, and this candidate combines both features.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~6 eV), electronically insulating lithium-ion conductor. Its phosphate framework is oxidatively robust toward LiCoO2 at 4.0 V, and it is chemically compatible with the sulfide electrolyte Li6PS5Cl. It is a well-studied cathode coating in sulfide-based cells, so it is a strong first candidate for a low interfacial penalty.

Li3BO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich borate. It should be oxidatively stable against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V and chemically tolerant of Li6PS5Cl, with a low expected interfacial penalty. It is a different chemical family from the earlier phosphate choice, so it tests whether a borate framework gives a lower penalty than the phosphate.
proposal.motivation: Earlier evaluation of Li3PO4 (phosphate, wide gap, Li-rich, oxidatively robust) suggested that Li-rich, wide-gap oxyanion coatings are reasonable for this interface; the borate family was not yet tested.

proposal.hypothesis: Li8ZrO6 is a Li-rich, wide-gap, electronically insulating zirconate. Zr4+ is hard to reduce or oxidize, so the framework should resist oxidation against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. Its high Li content favors Li-ion transport and chemical compatibility with Li6PS5Cl. With about seven non-Li atoms per formula unit, the reaction penalty per non-Li atom may be diluted relative to simpler oxides such as Li2O.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 and Li3BO3 proposals pointed to Li-rich, wide-gap oxyanion coatings. Their results are not shown, so this choice is a different chemical family (zirconate) that tests whether a Li-rich transition-metal oxide gives a lower penalty.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich fluoride with very high oxidative stability, so it should resist decomposition against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. It is also a common protective interphase component in sulfide cells. Fluoride frameworks are generally less reactive toward Li6PS5Cl than oxides, so this should give a low interfacial penalty. The halide family has not been tested yet.
proposal.motivation: Earlier proposals covered phosphate, borate, and zirconate oxide coatings, which share a Li-rich, wide-gap oxyanion design. A fluoride tests a different chemical family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li8SiO6 is a Li-rich orthosilicate with a wide band gap, so it should be electronically insulating. Si4+ is hard to oxidize, so the framework should resist decomposition against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. Its high Li content favors Li-ion transport and compatibility with Li6PS5Cl. With six O and one Si per formula unit, the penalty per non-Li atom may be diluted relative to simpler oxides such as Li2O.

Li6Si2O7 is a Li-rich, wide-gap, electronically insulating silicate. Si4+ resists oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2, and the high Li content favors compatibility with Li6PS5Cl. It has about nine non-Li atoms per formula unit, so the per-atom penalty may be diluted relative to Li2O. It is a close analogue of the evaluated Li8SiO6 with a higher silica fraction.
proposal.motivation: Earlier evaluated Li8SiO6 (Li-rich orthosilicate, wide gap, Si4+ oxidatively robust) suggests silicate frameworks are a reasonable coating family. Li6Si2O7 tests whether a more silica-rich, non-Li-dilute composition lowers the penalty.

proposal.hypothesis: Li6Zr2O7 is a Li-rich, wide-gap, electronically insulating zirconate. Zr4+ is hard to oxidize or reduce, so the framework should resist decomposition against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. Its high Li content favors Li-ion transport and compatibility with Li6PS5Cl. With nine non-Li atoms per formula unit, the per-atom penalty should be diluted relative to Li2O, and it is available in the candidate list, unlike the Li8ZrO6 composition.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li8ZrO6 zirconate proposal (Li-rich, Zr4+ oxidatively robust, wide gap) suggested Li-rich zirconates are a promising coating family; Li6Zr2O7 is the closest available analogue.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich oxide with high oxidative stability near 4 V, so it should resist decomposition against LiCoO2. It is a different chemical family (simple oxide) from the phosphate, borate, zirconate, fluoride, and silicate choices already tested. Its very high Li content should favor Li-ion transport and compatibility with Li6PS5Cl. The per-atom penalty is less diluted than in larger formulas, so the result will show whether a simple oxide beats the complex oxyanion coatings.
proposal.motivation: Earlier proposals covered phosphate, borate, zirconate, fluoride, and silicate coatings, all of which are Li-rich wide-gap compositions. The other-oxide family has not been tested, so Li2O tests that family.

proposal.hypothesis: LiZr2(PO4)3 combines a phosphate framework, which is oxidatively robust against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V and chemically compatible with Li6PS5Cl, with Zr4+, which resists both oxidation and reduction. It should be wide-gap and electronically insulating, and its NASICON-type structure provides Li-ion conduction. It sits between the earlier Li3PO4 phosphate and Li6Zr2O7 zirconate proposals, so it tests whether a mixed Zr-phosphate beats them on interfacial penalty.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 (phosphate, oxidatively robust, compatible with sulfide) and Li6Zr2O7/Li8ZrO6 (Zr4+, Li-rich, wide gap) proposals pointed to phosphate and zirconate frameworks as promising for this interface.
